reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows consolidated GAAP profitability and company-defined core earnings higher, with net investment income also higher, while the business insurance segment shows lower written premiums and lower reported and underlying underwriting gain alongside a higher reported and underlying combined ratio. Personal insurance shows higher GAAP net income and higher reported underwriting gain with a lower reported combined ratio, but its underlying underwriting gain is lower and its underlying combined ratio higher, so the reported improvement is not matched by the underlying measure. The catastrophe ratio is lower in both segments while favorable prior-year development is smaller in business insurance, so the segment results mix a benign current-accident-year catastrophe load with reduced reserve benefit; the selected rows do not establish which driver dominates or why. The tax line is a positive expense in both periods and is not treated as a smaller tax drag. All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic on selected rows, not year-over-year, not guidance versus realized results, and not causal attribution; no valuation or trade conclusion is drawn. Because the selected extract lacks the underlying loss ratio, expense ratio, premium rate and exposure detail, reserve development amounts, investment income composition, prior-year comparatives and any management guidance, the drivers of the reported improvement cannot be verified and the research state is held for review rather than advanced.
